keyFindings.description: linger's 'timeout' exit returns at the floor without checking a successor that took the record but is not receiving yet. The deadline is set before the flush and the release (handBack), so with both at their bounds (1 s, 2 s; the 10.25 s case the implementer documents) the deadline has passed when linger starts, and at 1.25 s it returns 'timeout' although a pod that took the record inside the 1.0 s window counts as handed back and holds only 3 s. Messages that reach the deliver subject in the gap go to a lost binding alone or meet the send-queue loss receive.go names, return at the 6 s ack wait, and arrive after newer ones. The round-4 comment asked to cover the timeout exit.

Release selects on done and ctx.Done() together. When handBack's own Release timed out (2 s) and the receiver's stop then overran its 10 s share (which the linger floor now allows, 10.25 s), Stop's second Release runs with an expired ctx after done has closed; Go picks either case at random, so half the time it returns ctx.Err() without letGo and the record is left to expire: a standby takes it after the TTL with the 7 s cap instead of a graceful hand-back. When the first release did succeed, the same pick logs a false 'listener lease not released' WARN. Check done before ctx.

RaiseMaxAge treats MaxAge 0 (no limit) as shorter than the target and lowers an unlimited bucket to 20 min, against its own doc; it also copies raiseReplicas' read-compare-update and drops its refusal naming, and its returned duration is unused.
